newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels say advancing on next targets.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels say advancing on next targets.

text.p: Zairean rebels said on Saturday they had pushed to within 200 km (125 miles) of Zaire's second city Lubumbashi and 100 km (60 miles) of the diamond capital of Mbuji-Mayi.

Rebel Voice of the People radio, broadcasting from the city of Goma, did not say where exactly they had reached in the thrust towards Lubumbashi, Zaire's copper and cobalt mining capital in Shaba province.
"They (rebels) have no time to waste given their task," it said.

In the northeastern capital of Kisangani, rebel leader Laurent Kabila told a rally since the city's fall last weekend his forces had seized Kabinda, 100 km (60 miles) east of the diamond capital Mbujui-Mayi in central Kasai province and had also captured Yangambi, 100 km (60 miles) west of Kisangani.
The rebels have set Lubumbashi and Mbuji-Mayi as their next major targets in their six month war to topple ailing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko and ruled out a ceasefire before negotiations.
Opposition to Mobutu's government runs high in mineral-rich Shaba province in the south which has fought several times in vain for secession during Mobutu's 32 years in power in Zaire.
